title: Continuation vs. Reversal
hook: Not every pullback is a reversal.

launchpad.outcome: Read a move against the structure as continuation, potential shift, or not enough information, based on which levels actually broke.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Price is pulling back in a bullish structure. Is it a reversal?

slides.title: Not every pullback is a reversal.
slides.body: Price moves against the structure. Three honest reads:

check.prompt: Price is pulling back inside a bullish structure. Nothing relevant has broken. Which read fits?

options.label: Reversal
options.feedback: A pullback alone isn’t a reversal. No relevant swing has broken.

options.label: Not enough information
options.why: ✓ Exactly. You don’t have to force a directional conclusion before price gives you enough evidence.

options.label: Continuation
options.feedback: Continuation needs a break of the prior high. Price hasn’t done that yet.

slides.title: Continuation, shift, or not enough yet?

steps.text: Bullish structure. Price just made a higher high. The prior HH and the supporting HL are marked.
Price pulls back and closes below an internal low.

asks.prompt: Continuation, potential shift, or not enough information?

options.label: Continuation
options.feedback: Price hasn’t broken the prior HH. Nothing has proved continuation yet.

options.label: Potential shift
options.feedback: Only an internal low broke. The supporting HL is still intact.

asks.hint: Which of the marked levels has price actually closed through?

steps.text: Price holds above the supporting HL and turns back up.

asks.prompt: What does the supporting HL holding tell you?

options.label: Continuation is confirmed
options.feedback: Holding isn’t breaking. The prior HH is still above price.

options.label: The bullish structure is still intact
options.why: Yes. The swing holding up the bullish structure wasn’t broken. That keeps the bullish story intact, but price hasn’t proved continuation yet.

options.label: Price is reversing
options.feedback: Nothing that supports the bullish structure has broken.

options.label: Continuation
options.why: Price just proved it progressed with the existing structure: a close through the prior HH. Bullish BOS, continuation information.

options.label: Potential shift
options.feedback: Price broke a high in the same direction as the bullish structure. That’s with the structure, not against it.

options.label: Not enough information
options.feedback: Price has now given you the evidence: a close through the prior HH.

slides.title: This time the supporting HL gives way.

steps.text: Bullish structure again. Watch the supporting HL.

evidence.conclusion: Change information: the bullish structure may be transitioning

asks.prompt: Continuation, potential shift, or not enough information?

options.label: Continuation
options.feedback: Price broke a low against the bullish structure. That isn’t continuation.

options.label: Potential shift
options.why: Price closed through the swing supporting the bullish structure, against its direction. Potential shift: change information.

options.label: Not enough information
options.feedback: You do have evidence here: the supporting HL was closed through.

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: One break suggests the structure may be transitioning. It doesn’t confirm what comes next.

options.label: No. It’s change information. Watch what price builds next
options.why: Exactly. The old story is in question. The new one isn’t written yet.

slides.title: Continuation, potential shift, or not enough?
slides.body: Check the marked levels. Don’t force a call price hasn’t earned.

items.why: Price closed through the prior HH with the bullish structure. Continuation information.
Pulling back, but neither the prior HH nor the supporting HL has broken. Not enough information yet.
Price closed through the supporting HL, against the bullish structure. Potential shift.
Bouncing inside a bearish structure, but no relevant level has broken. Not enough information yet.
Price closed through the prior LL with the bearish structure. Continuation information.
Price closed through the supporting LH, against the bearish structure. Potential shift.

slides.passText: You’re weighing evidence, not guessing direction.

slides.label: Core principle
slides.quote: “I don’t know yet” is sometimes the most technically correct answer.

slides.prompt: Why isn’t every pullback a reversal?
slides.modelAnswer: Because a pullback is just price moving against the structure for a while. Inside a bullish structure, price can pull back and even break internal lows while the supporting HL holds. Until a relevant swing breaks, the honest answer is often “not enough information yet.” A close through the supporting swing gives change information. A close through the prior high gives continuation information.

takeaways: A pullback alone is not a reversal.
A close through the prior high gives continuation information. A close through the supporting swing gives change information.
“Not enough information yet” is often the most accurate read.
remember: I don’t know yet is sometimes the most technically correct answer.
